description: Rick travels by barge and road from Bordeaux through the canals of south-west France to the Mediterranean and Marseille, using markets, village kitchens, wine country and regional dishes to trace the changing food landscape along the route.

s03e01.description: Rick leaves Padstow for Bordeaux and the waterways of south-west France, beginning a barge journey with market produce, artichokes, poached eggs and eels cooked in cider.

s03e02.description: Following the Garonne away from Bordeaux, Rick explores the food of the river and surrounding countryside, from eels with parsley and garlic to petit salé, duck and the robust cooking of Gascony.

s03e03.description: The Canal Latéral à la Garonne carries Rick toward Agen, where celebrated prunes, snails and the produce of the south-west become an excuse to examine why seemingly humble regional foods endure.

s03e04.description: On the barge from Agen toward Moissac, Rick digs further into Gascon cooking and the markets of the Tarn-et-Garonne, including the restorative simplicity of poule au pot.

s03e05.description: River Tarn pike, duck confit with red cabbage and a visit to a Moissac chef mark the approach to Toulouse, where waterways, farms and restaurant kitchens keep converging on the plate.

s03e06.description: Toulouse sausage leads naturally toward Castelnaudary and the fierce local pride surrounding cassoulet, as Rick examines how beans, preserved meats and patient cooking became a regional identity.

s03e07.description: Travelling deeper along the Canal du Midi, Rick visits a Foreign Legion canteen and encounters North African flavours alongside southern French cooking, including tagine, roast kid and tripe.

s03e08.description: The journey reaches Narbonne and the Mediterranean, where grilled sardines, local white pudding, honey and squid-ink pasta signal the shift from inland Gascony to coastal Languedoc.

s03e09-10.description: The final stretch reaches the Étang de Thau for oysters and mussels and catches Sète in the energy of Bastille Day and water jousting, before continuing through Aigues-Mortes to Marseille for black bream, bouillabaisse and the seafood of the Mediterranean.
